entry.description: Linear-error clique partitions of split graphs. The primary source reports: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the main results of the author's preprint "Linear-Error Clique Partitions of Split Graphs via Structured Triangle Packing" (Erdős #81 series, Paper III): there is an absolute constant C such that every finite split graph G on n vertices satisfies |E(G)| − 2ν₃(G) ≤ n²/6 + C·n, where ν₃(G) is the maximum number of pairwise edge-disjoint triangles (Theorem 1.1); consequently G has a clique partition (a family of cliques covering every edge exactly once) with at most n²/6 + C·n cliques (Corollary 1.2). The quadratic coefficient 1/6 is the sharp one for split graphs. The constant C is existential and not explicit. Two ingredients of the proof, the asymptotic gap between fractional and integral triangle packings and exact triangle decompositions of dense triangle-divisible graphs, are taken from two registered formalizations (see related_formalizations). entry.description: CONDITIONAL on Perelli-Pintz-Salerno 1984 and Perelli-Pintz 1993: Halupczok's ternary Goldbach mean value theorem with primes in progressions and short intervals, repaired. The primary source reports: CONDITIONAL on two cited results, both taken as explicit hypotheses of the theorems and never as axioms: PPS1984Remark, the printed Remark on p. 530 of A. Perelli, J. Pintz and S. Salerno, Bombieri's theorem in short intervals, 1984, and PP1993Goldbach, the Goldbach analogue of Theorem 3 of A. Perelli and J. Pintz, On the exceptional set for Goldbach's problem in short intervals, 1993, established in its sections 3 to 5 but not printed as a numbered theorem. These are the inputs that the paper's own proof quotes as its Theorems 2.1 and 2.3. PP1993Goldbach is therefore a weaker citation than a numbered theorem: it is the unnumbered Goldbach analogue that Halupczok says the proof of Perelli and Pintz can be adapted to give, stated here in the general form that argument yields. Under the two hypotheses, a complete Lean 4 proof of a repaired form of Theorem 1.2 of K. Halupczok, Goldbach's problem with primes in arithmetic progressions and in short intervals, J. Theor. Nombres Bordeaux 25, 2013, 331 to 351: summed over moduli q <= Q, the weighted count of p1 + p2 + p3 = n with p1 = a mod q and p1, p2 in short intervals differs from its singular series main term T(n, q, a) Y1 Y2 by << Y1 Y2 L^-A. As printed, the theorem sums over all q <= Q with the printed T, which does not vanish when a and q have a common factor, while the prime sum then is empty, so the printed statement fails, for example at a = 3, q = 3. The repair takes the main term to be 0 for such q, or equivalently restricts to q coprime to a. The entry also proves that the two hypotheses imply the paper's Theorems 2.1 and 2.3, as derived results of this entry. Perelli, J. Pintz and S. Salerno, Bombieri's theorem in short intervals, 1984, and PP1993Goldbach, the Goldbach analogue of Theorem 3 of A. Perelli and J. Pintz, On the exceptional set for Goldbach's problem in short intervals, 1993, established in its sections 3 to 5 but not printed as a numbered theorem. These are the inputs that the paper's own proof quotes as its Theorems 2.1 and 2.3. PP1993Goldbach is therefore a weaker citation than a numbered theorem: it is the unnumbered Goldbach analogue that Halupczok says the proof of Perelli and Pintz can be adapted to give, stated here in the general form that argument yields. Under the two hypotheses, a complete Lean 4 proof of a repaired form of Theorem 1.2 of K. Halupczok, Goldbach's problem with primes in arithmetic progressions and in short intervals, J. Theor. Nombres Bordeaux 25, 2013, 331 to 351: summed over moduli q <= Q, the weighted count of p1 + p2 + p3 = n with p1 = a mod q and p1, p2 in short intervals differs from its singular series main term T(n, q, a) Y1 Y2 by << Y1 Y2 L^-A. As printed, the theorem sums over all q <= Q with the printed T, which does not vanish when a and q have a common factor, while the prime sum then is empty, so the printed statement fails, for example at a = 3, q = 3. The repair takes the main term to be 0 for such q, or equivalently restricts to q coprime to a. The entry also proves that the two hypotheses imply the paper's Theorems 2.1 and 2.3, as derived results of this entry. Binary Goldbach is open and is not claimed; ternary Goldbach is a theorem of Helfgott. entry.description: Zero-Sum Quartet Incidence and Sharp Maximal-Independent-Set Witnesses on Eight Vertices. The primary source reports: We prove an exact four-term probability law for zero-sum maximal-independent-set witnesses. For every connected simple graph G on eight vertices and every admissible eight-point cap U in F_3^3, sample uniformly from all 40,320 bijections of the vertices onto U. Let N0 count zero-sum maximal independent four-sets, m count the size-four maximal independent sets, n0 and n2 count their unordered pairs intersecting in zero and two vertices, and h count compatible unordered triples. Put M1 = 2m/35, M2 = 2n0/35 + n2/315, and M3 = h/315. Then P(N0=0) = 1-M1+M2-M3, P(N0=1) = M1-2M2+3M3, P(N0=2) = M2-3M3, and P(N0=3) = M3 = h/315 <= 1/105; equality holds if and only if G is isomorphic to the spider S(2,2,2,1). In particular N0 <= 3. entry.description: A prespecified betting test of panmixia against a two-deme history: size and power. entry.description: An upper bound on the denominators of solutions of the two-locus sampling recursion. The primary source reports: This entry formalizes degree and divisibility facts about the denominators of solutions to the two-locus sampling recursion with two alleles at each locus. Centred moments of a solution, grouped in blocks by the numbers i and j of lineages at the two loci, satisfy a tridiagonal linear system with matrix T(i, j) whose right-hand side involves only smaller blocks. An explicit product D of linear factors in the mutation rates and of block determinants E(p, s) = det T(p, s) clears the denominator of the solution: D times the solution lies in any subring that contains the parameters. Conditionally on D being the reduced denominator of the top centred moment, every denominator of the solution is divisible by E. The determinant E(i, j) has degree min(i, j) in the recombination rate when a nonvanishing condition holds, and is positive when i, j ≥ 2 and the rates are nonnegative. Two statements show that the diagonal determinants E(m, m), with one mutation rate set to zero, have irreducible factors of unbounded degree as m varies, both as polynomials in the mutation rate over rational functions of the recombination rate and as polynomials in the recombination rate over rational functions of the mutation rate. An explicit product D of linear factors in the mutation rates and of block determinants E(p, s) = det T(p, s) clears the denominator of the solution: D times the solution lies in any subring that contains the parameters. Conditionally on D being the reduced denominator of the top centred moment, every denominator of the solution is divisible by E. The determinant E(i, j) has degree min(i, j) in the recombination rate when a nonvanishing condition holds, and is positive when i, j ≥ 2 and the rates are nonnegative. Two statements show that the diagonal determinants E(m, m), with one mutation rate set to zero, have irreducible factors of unbounded degree as m varies, both as polynomials in the mutation rate over rational functions of the recombination rate and as polynomials in the recombination rate over rational functions of the mutation rate.

entry.description: An explicit block-recursive formula for solutions of the two-locus sampling recursion. The primary source reports: This entry formalizes an explicit block-recursive formula for the solution of the two-locus sampling recursion under parent-independent mutation, with two alleles at each locus, positive mutation rates, and nonnegative recombination rate, over any ordered field. The explicit expression equals every solution of the recursion and is itself a solution, so it is the unique solution. Lumping statements show that merging alleles, by pushing configurations forward along maps between allele sets of any sizes, carries solutions to solutions, and that when every allele class is merged into two classes the lumped values are given by the explicit two-allele formula at the merged allele frequencies. A variant of the explicit formula, for any number of alleles at one locus and two at the other, is shown to equal every solution of the recursion. entry.description: Block determinants of the two-locus sampling recursion: degree, positivity, squarefreeness, coprimality, and Galois groups. The primary source reports: This entry formalizes algebraic properties of the block determinants E(i, j) of the two-locus sampling recursion, viewed as polynomials in the recombination rate ρ. E(i, j) is the determinant of an explicit (min(i, j) + 1)-square tridiagonal matrix whose entries depend on i, j, the mutation rates θ_A and θ_B, and ρ. Its degree in ρ is min(i, j) under a stated nondegeneracy condition, and it is positive for i, j ≥ 2 with nonnegative parameters. For nonnegative real mutation rates, every root in ρ of E(5, 5) and of E(7, 7) is real and negative. At explicit rational parameters with negative θ_A, E(5, 5) and E(7, 7) are irreducible over the rationals, have 3 and 5 real roots, have Galois groups of orders 120 and 5040 (the full symmetric groups), and have roots that are not expressible by radicals. E(5, 5) and E(7, 7) are irreducible over the field of rational functions in the mutation rate, and their Galois groups over the field of rational functions in two independent mutation rates are the full symmetric groups; a general specialization lemma used for this is also stated. Squarefreeness, and coprimality for distinct index pairs, of the determinants with i, j ≥ 1 are stated over a field of rational functions in two independent mutation rates and over a field of Laurent series in which both mutation rates are large with a ratio that is not rational. entry.description: Linked-pair panels: panel laws are determined by finitely many Laplace values. The primary source reports: This entry formalizes panels of linked site pairs observed through a reporting channel, with the pair coalescence time T following a probability law on the non-negative reals. All L sites of a panel share the same time T; given T = t, the sites are reported independently, and at each site the two lineages share one latent type with weight e^(−kt) and have independent types otherwise, each type being reported through a channel that maps K latent types to probability distributions on a finite set of labels. For an informative channel (one whose rows are not all equal) and a panel of length L, the panel laws of two time laws agree for all outcomes if and only if their Laplace transforms agree at the points rk for r = 0, …, L. If the channel erases all information, every panel law agrees. If the transforms agree up to L and differ at the next point, then panels of length L agree but some panel of length L + 1 differs. All L sites of a panel share the same time T; given T = t, the sites are reported independently, and at each site the two lineages share one latent type with weight e^(−kt) and have independent types otherwise, each type being reported through a channel that maps K latent types to probability distributions on a finite set of labels. For an informative channel (one whose rows are not all equal) and a panel of length L, the panel laws of two time laws agree for all outcomes if and only if their Laplace transforms agree at the points rk for r = 0, …, L. If the channel erases all information, every panel law agrees. If the transforms agree up to L and differ at the next point, then panels of length L agree but some panel of length L + 1 differs. For k > 0, agreement of all panels of all lengths is equivalent to equality of the time laws.

entry.description: No formula with denominators of bounded degree, in the total mutation parameter or in rho, for the two-locus sampling recursion. The primary source reports: This entry formalizes results on the degree of denominators of any closed-form expression for the solution of the two-locus sampling recursion of the coalescent with recombination, with two alleles at each locus and parent-independent mutation. The mutation rates, the recombination rate rho, and the allele frequencies are independent indeterminates, and the recursion is solved over a field of rational functions in them. An expression is built from rational constants, arbitrary coefficients from the coefficient field, the rates, sums, products, and quotients; it is admissible at degree D when every divisor evaluates to a nonzero polynomial of degree at most D in a designated variable (rho, or the total mutation rate theta_A + theta_B). A closure lemma shows that admissible expressions in inputs with bounded denominators have bounded denominators. For the sample of two lineages that carry the same haplotype at both loci, no admissible expression of degree one in rho, and none of degree two in the total mutation rate, equals the value of the solution; variants bound the total degree of the divisors in the three rates instead. For the samples of m lineages typed at locus A only and m typed at locus B only, all of allele 0, for every bound D there is an m ≥ 2 at which no admissible expression of degree D, in the total mutation rate or in rho, equals the value of the solution. entry.description: A partition-pair decomposition of the two-locus sampling probability with Ewens marginals. The primary source reports: This entry formalizes a decomposition of the two-locus sampling probability, under finite-allele parent-independent mutation, in terms of pairs of set partitions of the sample, with Ewens marginals at each locus. A partition-carrying ancestral process with coalescence, mutation, and recombination records, at each locus, which sample members lose their ancestry to the same mutation; the kernel is the probability that it ends with a given pair of partitions. The solution of the two-locus sampling recursion at a fully typed sample is the sum over pairs of partitions of the kernel times the probability that each block receives a single allele consistent with the sample. Summing the kernel over the partition at one locus gives the Ewens partition probability at the other; as the recombination rate tends to infinity the kernel tends to the product of the two Ewens partition probabilities; and with recombination rate 0 the common refinement of the two partitions has the Ewens law with parameter θA + θB. The sampling probability equals the product of its one-locus marginals for all parameter values exactly when at most one lineage is typed at one of the loci (with at least two alleles per locus). A closed form for configurations with two lineages typed at each locus is also stated, together with existence of a solution of the recursion. entry.description: Total variation bound between an unpruned ancestral recombination process and SMC' on pairwise coalescence times. The primary source reports: This entry formalizes a total variation bound between the pairwise coalescence-time process of an unpruned ancestral recombination graph and the SMC' approximation, for N ≥ 1 samples, a unit-length genome, and scaled recombination rate R ≥ 0. The observed object is the collection of pairwise coalescence times of all sample pairs at every rational position in [0, 1). The total variation distance is at most an explicit double bound, which is at most min(1, R² times a quadratic coefficient in N − 1). The distance is 0 for one sample and for zero recombination. Supporting statements show that the event kernels of both processes are Markov, the two laws are probability measures, the number of live lineages of the backward process reaches at most one almost surely, the observed coalescence times are almost surely finite, and the expected number of active events, the expected total time, and the expected largest observed coalescence time are bounded by an explicit absorption budget. entry.description: When one finite block of linked sites separates a three-sample genealogy from every panmictic history. The primary source reports: This entry formalizes conditions under which a single finite block of linked sites separates a three-sample genealogy from every panmictic history. A law of the two coalescence-interval lengths and the tree shape of three sampled sequences is uniformly separated at mutation scale k > 0 when some block of L completely linked sites, observed under the equal-rates mutation model, has a law at ℓ1 distance at least a fixed ε > 0 from the block law of every panmictic history (any nonnegative, locally integrable, time-varying coalescence rate with a diverging integrated clock), at every mutation scale and for every alphabet size K ≥ 2. For laws with nonnegative interval lengths, a positive first coalescence time, and a regular first-survival profile matching the first coalescence time, uniform separation holds if and only if the law differs from the panmictic law with the profile's rate, in which the tree shape is uniform and independent of the times; a version for laws of the interval lengths alone, with a uniform independent shape, is also given. For three-sample symmetric island histories with time-varying coalescence and migration rates under the stated integrability hypotheses, uniform separation holds if and only if the history is not the one with all three lineages starting in the same island, no migration, and a diverging integrated coalescence clock. For finite-phase histories, separation is equivalent to failure of a density identity characterizing the panmictic form.
